en: Oṃ, homage to all the Yoginīs of all accomplishments! Homage to all the Mothers of all accomplishments!
Homage to the Blessed Lady Caṇḍakāpālinī, the Mistress of the entire wheel of families, who is gladdened by eternal, arisen bliss!
Oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hrāṃ pheṃ kṣoṃ kroṃ, homage!

Oṃ khphreṃ! O Goddess who bestows the path to Nirvāṇa, O Supreme Haṃsinī; O pacifier of calamities and misfortunes, O destroyer of all evils, enemies, and afflictions; O ferry across the ocean of all disasters, O subduer of all foes; O Goddess, come, come! Laugh, laugh! Vagla, vagla!
O devourer of human blood, entrails, and fat! O crusher of my enemies, crush them!
Eat, eat! Pierce, pierce with the trident! Cut, cut with the sword! Strike, strike! Sever, sever!
Accomplish, accomplish all my desires until they are fully realized, O Most Compassionate One!

O Blessed One, who assumes the form of Mahābhairava; O Goddess saluted by the best of the thirty [gods], whose hair is the mass of all mantras, who is the beloved of those who bow before you; O Great Kālī, destroyer of Time! Khphreṃ Kṣrīṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ! Be gracious, O incomparable Madanā! Act, act!
*Surāsura-kanyakā hrīṃ śrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. This is the *mālā-mantra*.
Auspiciousness.
Oṃ. Homage to the illustrious Gaṇeśa; homage!
Salutations to Śrī Parāya.
The Goddess said:
O Maheśvarī, by your grace, I have heard all the secrets.
Now I wish to hear that which is called the Varmapratyagīrā. || 1 ||
The illustrious Lord said:
O beloved, Queen Tamā is dearer to me than my own life.
Your words are not in vain; they bring about life for all living beings.
O steadfast one, I shall speak words that ought not to be spoken, even unto you.
By merely donning this armor, one becomes manifest as Bhairava himself. || 3 ||
One should always recite this merit-armor that provides all protection.
There is no mantra superior to this for providing protection to the self. || 4 ||
It is timely, endowed with great potency, and produces immediate conviction.
O Goddess, one should meditate first for the sake of accomplishing all desires and goals. || 5 ||
Her body is as white as milk, a jasmine flower, or the moon, and she has five faces with three eyes on each.
She was exceedingly gentle, with a beautiful face, and held ten uplifted staffs.
A sword, a skull-topped staff, a trident, a skull-bowl, and a noose of kuśa grass.
Holding the elephant-goad and the bell in her hands, she is divinely beautiful.
Clad in silken garments of the finest quality, she was adorned with divine armlets.
In that void [is the form] of that Great Lord, who has one face and two arms.
The Great Goddess resides in the body, bestowing sovereignty over the three worlds.
Situated in the midst of the eight Mātṛkās, she stands upon five corpses.

Of this Kavaca of Śrīpatyāgirādevī, Nārāyaṇa is the seer (ṛṣi), Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ), Pratyagirā Śrīsiddhilakṣmī is the deity (devatā), Hrīṃ is the seed-syllable (bīja), Khphreṃ is the power (kīlaka), and Phreṃ Svāhā is for the purpose of my protection of all limbs; thus is the application (viniyoga) in recitation.
May he always protect the station of the young brahmin for me, O son of noble family.
O protector of the Kshatriyas, O youth, O destroyer of the Kshatriya obstacles, O warder-off of impediments!
O great hero, seated upon the throne, you are a protector of the realm and possessed of great strength.
Together with the Yoginīs, my auspicious protection is to be known as eternal. || 11 ||
To the east, however, one should worship Bhairavī, Śyāmā, and Gaurī, as well as Brahmāṇī.
May the fierce Kaumārī, who possesses the brilliance of fire and the luster of a sword, protect you here from Dakṣa.
Krodhavaiṣṇavī is in the southwest, and Vārāhī, intoxicated with pride, is in the west.
May Kapālī, together with Śakrānī, always protect [us] from the northwest. || 13 ||
Kroṃ.
May the goddess Carcikā Bhiṣaṇā protect in the northern direction.
May Mahācaṇḍinī, the Great Delighting One, protect [me] in the northeastern direction. || 14 ||
May Mahāmāyā protect above; may Kulanāsinī protect below.
Thus ends the root mantra.
Oṃ.
Oṃ Siddhilakṣmī, may you, the all-protecting one, grant me the eternal Brahman. || 15 ||
Viśvalakṣmī is on the forehead, and Bhujaṅgapāpahālinī is on the [forehead].
The Brahman-lakṣmī, the bestower of Brahman, protects [the practitioner] between the eyebrows. || 16 ||
The eyes are the splendor of majesty, and at the end of evil, she is the embodiment of light.
Protecting the pair of ears with the beauty of green grass, she pervades the sky. || 17 ||
May the beauty of fragrance protect the two nostrils with a white spear from the earth.
The splendor of touch, moving within the atmosphere, protected those who travel through the sky. || 18 ||
The pair of cheeks is Mahālakṣmī, who dwells within the lunar orb.
Prosperity resides on the upper lip during the day, while misfortune dwells upon the other at night.
May the tooth in the middle of the upper row of teeth always protect the auspicious fortune of merit.
The Fortune of Taste dwells in the waters of the field of the human body. || 20 ||
O Sarasvatī, you whose root is the eternal *alakṣa* (the unmanifest), you who are the universal fortune!
The mantra-goddess at the root of the ear, together with her conch, grants all desires. || 21 ||
The Ghaṭikā protects the neck, bestows the fortune of a hero, and is all-auspicious.
And let Mudrālakṣmī and Vakudakaṇṭhā be swift in their speed. || 22 ||
And may the royal fortune always protect the heart, O Bhadrakaṇṭha.
Bāhuka, Rakṣa, Khikhaṇi, Kuryalā, and Vidārikā; || 23 ||
The two hands are Yama and Jihvā, and the anus is Aparavālādanī.
May Bhairavī, who is worshipped by the universe, always protect the lord of men. || 24 ||
May she, who destroys fear in the Kali age, protect the breasts of Mudrālakṣmī.
May Ghaṇṭhāvāsā protect Kurigula on the left and right sides. || 25 ||
May the swift-moving Cauremātās always protect [us] from the claws of Karanakhā.
One should protect the two armpits with the owl-footed [mantra] and the armpits with the cakravāka [mantra]. || 26 ||
One should always protect against insects, worms, and small creatures on both sides.
May Kākatuṇḍī, the auspicious Caṇḍāmukhī, always protect [me] from behind.
The Ṭākāriṇī pierces the heart; she is the burning one.
Indeed, the fire always resides within the middle part above the stomach.
May Jayashvari, who holds a bell in her left hand, protect the middle of the belly with her three eyes.
O Śivārakṣa, do not be excessively distressed; O monkey, you shall become emaciated. || 29 ||
May Mahogrā protect the thighs, and may Kāminī protect the knees.
May the Goddess of the Discus, the sustainer of the world and the bestower of victory, protect us. || 30 ||
May Rudrāsanā protect the ankles; may Kāpālinī protect the calves.
Caṇḍakāpālinī shall protect [his] feet, and Kamalavāsinī [shall protect his] feet.
May the Goddess, who dwells upon the surface of the feet and resides in gold, protect [us].
May the soles of his feet protect [us], and may his toes protect the abodes of those abodes.
But Mother Dhāmnāmbā, who destroys sin, shall protect me from the toe-nails up to the feet.
O Goddess, the circle of the piercing ones, may your shadow protect me at all times. || 33 ||
And Raviprabhā Mahogrā, may they protect and guard the vanguard.
Vajreśī shines upon the back and the left side.
Bhageśvarī is in the south, and Vāḍaveśvarī is in the southeast.
Or she protects against the Rakṣasīs in the southwest, and Pāpanāśinī protects in the northwest. || 35 ||
May Īśvarī protect [me] in the northeast, and may Bhadradāyinī protect [me] above.
The goddess is the eternal support of the field, always present, the destroyer of Time.
I am Ūrdhvakeśinī; my body hairs and my hair are disheveled.
May Ḍākinī protect the skin-element, and Rākī protect the blood. || 37 ||
May Māsarakṣā and Lākinī protect [the practitioner], and may Medvarakṣā and Kāminī protect [him].
O Hākinī, protect my bones, elements, and marrow; O Hākinī, protect me! || 38 ||
May Yākinī and Śukladhātu protect [me] constantly and at all times.
Agāni, Kālarātrī, Pitta, and Jayamaṅgalā. || 40 ||
Prāṇa, apāna, udāna, samāna, and vyāna.
May Ukeśvarī always protect me; may Prānonmī protect me; may Tripurā protect me. 41.
Protect the virtues of all beings, O bearer of the slaying of Madhu and Kaiṭabha!
May Kālikā, ending with Mahākāla, protect me constantly from the beginning to the end.
May Mahāmāyā, who comprises the entire universe, eternally protect my dharma.
May Sundarī protect [him] with fame, renown, fortune, and sovereignty. 43.
She who protects the lineage, the cattle, and the children, and destroys Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.
One should protect one's sons from others; O Sarasvatī, one should protect one's wife.
May Mālinī protect [me] from the fire, and may Svapnasvapneśvarī guard me.
May Samaradevī protect [us] from sorcery, malevolent magic, and battle. || 45 ||
May Idā, Ugracaṇḍā, Piṅgarā, and Vaiṣṇavī protect [me] here.
May Suṣumnā protect the primordial nature (prakṛti), and may Cañcikā protect all the limbs. || 46 ||
In the royal family of Rana, a marriage festival was held.
May the Great Goddess, the pervasive Sovereign, protect the fortune of success eternally. || 47 ||
The Goddess seated upon five corpses protects every limb and everything.
May she who dwells by the Vindhya protect me in the forest, in the difficult terrain, and on the mountain peak.
May Bhairavī always protect [me] in the water, in the ocean, and in the river.
Thus has this armor been proclaimed, the means for accomplishing dharma, kama, and artha.
This is the supreme secret, the means for accomplishing all aims.
By reciting this, all sins are instantly destroyed; it is the "Pillar of Immediate Conviction. (50)
O God, recite this armor-mantra (*kavaca*), fashioned by Viṣṇu, which is divine and supreme.
O Lord, one obtains the fruit of every sacrifice; of this there is no doubt. || 51 ||
And the lion, O Mother, is the cause of victory in battles.
Just as fire exists within a reed, so too does the mantra-body always exist within the body.
No disease arises for him, nor does any suffering ever occur.
Even by that [bestowal of a boon], all suffering arises instead. || 53 ||
Through merit accumulated over many births, one may obtain that armor.
O Nābhāparatara, nothing exists that is superior to you within the lotus of the world.
O divine armor, listen to this great and meritorious fruit of the hymn.
One shall be liberated from the suffering of disease and become endowed with beauty and virtue. || 55 ||
For you, who are the destroyer of the flood of obstacles, no misfortunes shall ever arise; this is certain.
Diseases do not arise in him, yet he dies with his body broken. || 56 ||
All four kinds of living beings become his offspring.
One should recite with devotion for one year this armor (kavaca) composed by Viṣṇu.
Having completely conquered all enemies, one will certainly become a king of kings.
Therefore, O living being, this Sāla tree [mantra] should be recited with every effort. 58.
[Thus ends the Śrīsiddhilakṣmī-kavaca in the Śrītrailokyadāra. Auspiciousness.]
